name: Barbell bench press
setup: Flat bench, eyes under the bar. Grip roughly 1.5x shoulder width. Feet flat, planted wide.
posture: Shoulder blades pinched back and down into the bench. Chest up, slight natural arch in the lower back. Glutes stay in contact with the bench.
execution: Unrack and hold over the upper chest. Inhale, lower to mid-chest in about 2 seconds with elbows at 45 degrees to the torso. Touch lightly, press up and exhale through the top half.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows to 90 degrees, which strains the shoulder. Bouncing the bar off the chest. Lifting the hips off the bench.

name: Dumbbell bench press
setup: Flat bench. Sit with dumbbells on your thighs, then kick them up one at a time as you lie back.
posture: Shoulder blades retracted, chest up, feet flat and driving into the floor.
execution: Start with dumbbells above the chest, palms forward. Inhale and lower to chest level over 2 seconds, elbows at 45 degrees. Press up and slightly together, exhaling.
commonMistakes: Clashing the dumbbells together at the top, which drops the tension. Dropping too deep and overstretching the shoulder.

name: Machine chest press
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles sit level with your mid-chest. Feet flat on the floor.
posture: Back and head against the pad, shoulder blades pulled back, chest up.
execution: Inhale, press the handles forward until the arms are almost straight without locking out. Exhale on the press, return over 2 seconds under control.
commonMistakes: Setting the seat too high, which turns it into a shoulder press. Letting the shoulders roll forward at the end of the push.

name: Smith machine bench press
setup: Flat bench positioned so the bar path lines up with your mid-chest. Grip 1.5x shoulder width.
posture: Shoulder blades retracted and down, chest up, feet planted.
execution: Unrack with a wrist twist. Inhale and lower to mid-chest over 2 seconds, elbows at 45 degrees. Press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Placing the bench too far forward so the fixed bar path hits the neck. Relying on the fixed path and letting the shoulders go loose.

name: Push-up
setup: Hands flat on the floor just wider than the shoulders, at chest level. Legs straight, feet hip width.
posture: Body in one straight line from head to heels. Core braced, glutes squeezed, neck neutral with eyes on the floor a foot ahead.
execution: Inhale and lower until the chest is roughly a fist's height from the floor, elbows at 45 degrees. Press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Hips sagging or piling up. Flaring elbows straight out to the sides. Only going halfway down.

name: Wide-grip push-up
setup: Hands flat on the floor, roughly twice shoulder width, at chest level.
posture: Straight line from head to heels, core braced, glutes tight.
execution: Inhale and lower under control until the chest is just off the floor. Press up and exhale. Range of motion is shorter than a standard push-up.
commonMistakes: Going too wide, which stresses the shoulder joint for very little extra chest work. Letting the hips drop.

name: Cable chest press
setup: Pulleys set at chest height. Grab both handles, step forward into a split stance for stability.
posture: Chest up, shoulders back and down, core braced, front knee softly bent.
execution: Inhale, press both handles forward and slightly together until the arms are nearly straight. Exhale on the press, return slowly to a light stretch.
commonMistakes: Standing square with feet level, which makes you unstable. Letting the cables yank the arms back too fast.

name: Pec deck machine
setup: Set the seat so the handles are at chest height. Sit back with elbows on the pads or hands on the grips.
posture: Back flat against the pad, chest up, shoulder blades pulled back.
execution: Inhale, bring the pads together in front of the chest in a hugging arc. Squeeze for a beat, exhale, then return over 2 seconds to a stretch.
commonMistakes: Setting the start position so wide that the shoulders overstretch. Shrugging the shoulders up during the squeeze.

name: Dumbbell fly
setup: Flat bench, one dumbbell in each hand pressed above the chest, palms facing each other.
posture: Shoulder blades retracted, chest up, feet planted.
execution: Keep a fixed 10 to 15 degree bend in the elbows. Inhale and open the arms in a wide arc until you feel a chest stretch, roughly level with the bench. Exhale and hug back up.
commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows, which turns it into a press. Going too deep and straining the shoulder. Using far too much weight.

name: Cable crossover (mid pulley)
setup: Both pulleys at chest height. A handle in each hand, step forward into a split stance.
posture: Chest up, shoulders down, slight forward lean from the hips, core braced.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Inhale, then bring the hands together in front of the chest in a wide arc and exhale. Squeeze for a beat, return slowly to a stretch.
commonMistakes: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows. Standing too far back so tension disappears at the finish.

name: Barbell floor press
setup: Lie on the floor inside a rack, bar set low. Knees bent, feet flat. Grip 1.5x shoulder width.
posture: Shoulder blades pinched, chest up, glutes and upper back pressed into the floor.
execution: Inhale, lower until the upper arms rest lightly on the floor, elbows at 45 degrees. Pause for one second, press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the elbows off the floor. Letting the elbows flare wide at the bottom.

name: Dumbbell floor press
setup: Lie flat on the floor with a dumbbell in each hand, knees bent, feet flat.
posture: Shoulder blades pulled back into the floor, chest up, core braced.
execution: Inhale and lower until the triceps touch the floor, elbows at 45 degrees. Pause one second, press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Slamming the elbows down. Letting the dumbbells drift toward the head instead of staying over the chest.

name: Kettlebell floor press
setup: Lie on the floor with a kettlebell in each hand, bells resting on the back of the forearms. Knees bent.
posture: Wrists straight and stacked over the elbows, shoulder blades pinched, core braced.
execution: Inhale and lower until the triceps touch the floor. Pause one second, press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Letting the wrists bend back under the bell. Allowing the bells to bang the forearms on the way down.

name: Resistance band chest press
setup: Anchor the band at chest height behind you. A handle in each hand, step forward into a split stance until there is tension.
posture: Chest up, shoulders back and down, core braced.
execution: Inhale, press both handles forward and slightly together, exhaling. Squeeze the chest at full extension, then return over 2 seconds against the band.
commonMistakes: Letting the band snap the arms back. Standing too close to the anchor, leaving no tension at the start.

name: Plate press (Svend press)
setup: Stand tall holding a weight plate flat between both palms at chest height, fingers pointing forward.
posture: Chest up, shoulders back and down, core braced, feet shoulder width.
execution: Squeeze the palms hard into the plate throughout. Inhale, press the plate straight out until the arms are nearly straight, exhaling. Return slowly, keeping the squeeze.
commonMistakes: Loosening the inward squeeze, which is the entire point of the movement. Letting the plate drift down or up instead of straight out.

name: Incline barbell bench press
setup: Bench set to 30 degrees. Eyes under the bar, grip 1.5x shoulder width, feet flat.
posture: Shoulder blades retracted and down, chest up, hips on the bench.
execution: Unrack over the upper chest. Inhale and lower to just below the collarbone over 2 seconds, elbows at 45 degrees. Press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Setting the bench above 45 degrees, which shifts the work to the front delts. Bouncing the bar off the chest.

name: Incline dumbbell press
setup: Bench at 30 degrees. Sit with dumbbells on the thighs and kick them up as you lie back.
posture: Shoulder blades pinched back, chest up, feet flat and driving into the floor.
execution: Start with the dumbbells above the upper chest. Inhale and lower to chest level over 2 seconds, elbows at 45 degrees. Press up and slightly in, exhaling.
commonMistakes: Bench angle too steep, turning it into a shoulder press. Banging the dumbbells together at the top.

name: Incline machine chest press
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest, just below the collarbone.
posture: Back and head flat against the pad, shoulder blades back, chest up.
execution: Inhale, press the handles up and forward until nearly straight without locking out. Exhale on the press, return over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Seat set too low, which drags the work down to the mid-chest. Shoulders rolling forward at lockout.

name: Incline smith machine press
setup: Bench at 30 degrees under the bar, positioned so the fixed path meets your upper chest.
posture: Shoulder blades retracted, chest up, feet planted flat.
execution: Unrack with a wrist twist. Inhale and lower to the upper chest over 2 seconds, elbows at 45 degrees. Press and exhale.
commonMistakes: Misplacing the bench so the bar path hits the throat or the belly. Letting the fixed path do the stabilising while the shoulders go slack.

name: Incline dumbbell fly
setup: Bench at 30 degrees. Dumbbells pressed above the upper chest, palms facing each other.
posture: Shoulder blades pulled back, chest up, feet flat.
execution: Hold a fixed 10 to 15 degree elbow bend. Inhale and open the arms wide until you feel a stretch across the upper chest. Exhale and hug back up.
commonMistakes: Straightening and re-bending the elbows. Dropping the arms far below bench level and stressing the shoulder.

name: Low-to-high cable crossover
setup: Both pulleys at the lowest setting. A handle in each hand, step forward into a split stance.
posture: Chest up, shoulders back and down, slight forward lean, core braced.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Inhale, then sweep the hands up and together to about chin height, exhaling. Squeeze for a beat and lower slowly.
commonMistakes: Shrugging at the top so the traps take over. Bending the elbows and turning it into a press.

name: Feet-elevated push-up
setup: Feet on a bench or box roughly 30 to 60cm high. Hands flat on the floor just wider than the shoulders.
posture: Straight line from head to heels, core braced hard, glutes squeezed, neck neutral.
execution: Inhale and lower until the chest is a fist's height off the floor, elbows at 45 degrees. Press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag as the elevation makes it harder. Going too high too soon, which wrecks the line.

name: Incline cable press
setup: Incline bench at 30 degrees set between two pulleys, both at the lowest setting. A handle in each hand.
posture: Shoulder blades back, chest up, feet flat.
execution: Inhale, press both handles up and slightly together over the upper chest, exhaling. Return over 2 seconds to a stretch.
commonMistakes: Placing the bench too far forward so the cables pull from the wrong angle. Letting the handles drift apart at the top.

name: Reverse-grip bench press
setup: Flat bench, hands underhand at shoulder width. Have a spotter help unrack, since the grip is awkward.
posture: Shoulder blades retracted, chest up, wrists straight and stacked over the elbows.
execution: Inhale and lower to the lower chest with elbows tucked close to the ribs. Press up and exhale, driving toward the upper chest.
commonMistakes: Loose wrists under an underhand grip. Unracking alone, which is the riskiest moment of this lift.

name: Landmine press
setup: One end of a barbell in a landmine sleeve or a corner. Hold the free end at shoulder height in one or both hands.
posture: Half-kneeling or standing tall, chest up, core braced, hips square to the bar.
execution: Inhale, press the bar up and forward along its arc until the arm is nearly straight, exhaling. Lower over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Leaning back to help the press. Letting the hips twist toward the working arm.

name: Incline band press
setup: Anchor the band behind an incline bench set to 30 degrees, at roughly bench height. A handle in each hand.
posture: Shoulder blades back, chest up, feet flat.
execution: Inhale, press up and slightly together over the upper chest, exhaling at the top where band tension peaks. Return over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Letting the band snap the arms back. Anchoring too high so the resistance pulls straight down.

name: Decline barbell bench press
setup: Decline bench at 15 to 30 degrees, legs secured. Grip 1.5x shoulder width. Have a spotter for unracking.
posture: Shoulder blades retracted, chest up, head supported.
execution: Unrack over the lower chest. Inhale and lower to the lower chest over 2 seconds, elbows at 45 degrees. Press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Sitting up quickly afterwards while blood is pooled in the head. Bouncing the bar off the ribs.

name: Decline dumbbell press
setup: Decline bench at 15 to 30 degrees, legs hooked. Dumbbells passed up or kicked into place.
posture: Shoulder blades pinched, chest up, head supported on the bench.
execution: Start above the lower chest. Inhale and lower to chest level over 2 seconds, elbows at 45 degrees. Press up and slightly in, exhaling.
commonMistakes: Getting into position without help, which is where most decline injuries happen. Letting the dumbbells drift toward the head.

name: Chest dip
setup: Parallel bars, hands at your sides. Push up to a supported start with arms straight.
posture: Lean the torso forward about 30 degrees and keep it there. Chest up, shoulders down away from the ears, ankles crossed behind.
execution: Inhale and lower until the upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, elbows flaring slightly out. Press up and exhale, keeping the forward lean.
commonMistakes: Going deeper than shoulder comfort allows. Drifting upright mid-rep, which turns it into a triceps dip. Shrugging at the bottom.

name: Assisted chest dip machine
setup: Set the assistance weight, then kneel or stand on the pad with hands on the parallel bars.
posture: Torso leaned forward about 30 degrees, chest up, shoulders pulled down away from the ears.
execution: Inhale and lower until the upper arms are parallel to the floor. Press up and exhale. Remember: lower assistance weight means you are getting stronger.
commonMistakes: Bouncing off the pad for momentum. Letting the torso drift upright and shifting the work to the triceps.

name: High-to-low cable crossover
setup: Both pulleys at the highest setting. A handle in each hand, step forward into a split stance.
posture: Chest up, shoulders back and down, slight forward lean from the hips, core braced.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Inhale, sweep the hands down and together in front of the hips, exhaling. Squeeze a beat, return slowly to a stretch.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows into a pressdown, which makes it a triceps move. Standing too upright so the arc gets flat.

name: Decline machine press
setup: Set the seat so the handles sit level with your lower chest. Feet flat.
posture: Back flat against the pad, shoulder blades back, chest up.
execution: Inhale, press the handles forward and slightly down until nearly straight. Exhale on the press, return over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Seat too high, which turns it into a flat press. Locking the elbows hard at the end.

name: Hands-elevated push-up
setup: Hands on a bench or box roughly 30 to 60cm high, just wider than the shoulders. Feet on the floor, legs straight.
posture: Straight line from head to heels, core braced, glutes squeezed.
execution: Inhale and lower until the chest is just off the bench edge, elbows at 45 degrees. Press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips pike up because the movement is easier. Choosing a surface that slides or tips.

name: Decline dumbbell fly
setup: Decline bench at 15 to 30 degrees, legs hooked. Dumbbells pressed above the lower chest, palms facing.
posture: Shoulder blades retracted, chest up, head supported.
execution: Fixed 10 to 15 degree elbow bend. Inhale and open the arms wide to a chest stretch. Exhale and hug back up over the lower chest.
commonMistakes: Going too heavy on a movement with a long lever. Dropping the arms far past bench level.

name: Decline smith machine press
setup: Decline bench at 15 to 30 degrees under the bar, lined up so the fixed path meets the lower chest. Legs secured.
posture: Shoulder blades pinched, chest up, head supported.
execution: Unrack with a wrist twist. Inhale and lower to the lower chest over 2 seconds, elbows at 45 degrees. Press and exhale.
commonMistakes: Misaligning the bench so the fixed path lands on the ribs or throat. Rushing to sit up at the end of the set.

name: Pull-up
setup: Overhand grip on a fixed bar, hands roughly 1.5x shoulder width. Hang with arms straight, ankles crossed behind.
posture: Chest up and proud, shoulders pulled down away from the ears before the first inch of movement. Ribs down, core braced so the legs don't swing.
execution: Exhale and drive the elbows down and back until the chin clears the bar. Lower over 2 to 3 seconds to a full hang, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Kipping and swinging for momentum. Stopping halfway down instead of reaching a full hang. Shrugging into the ears at the bottom.

name: Chin-up
setup: Underhand grip on a fixed bar, hands about shoulder width. Hang with arms straight, ankles crossed.
posture: Chest up, shoulders pulled down away from the ears, ribs down, core braced.
execution: Exhale and pull the elbows down toward the ribs until the chin clears the bar. Lower over 2 to 3 seconds to a full hang, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Swinging the legs to generate momentum. Cutting the bottom short. Letting the elbows drift far forward, which turns it into a curl.

name: Assisted pull-up machine
setup: Set the assistance weight, then kneel or stand on the pad and take an overhand grip 1.5x shoulder width.
posture: Chest up, shoulders pulled down away from the ears, core braced so the pad doesn't bounce.
execution: Exhale and drive the elbows down and back until the chin clears the bar. Lower over 2 to 3 seconds. Less assistance weight means you are getting stronger.
commonMistakes: Bouncing off the pad at the bottom. Using so much assistance that the back barely works.

name: Lat pulldown
setup: Set the thigh pad snug. Overhand grip roughly 1.5x shoulder width. Sit with arms straight overhead.
posture: Chest up, slight backward lean of about 15 degrees, shoulders down, core braced.
execution: Exhale and pull the bar to the upper chest, driving the elbows down and back. Squeeze for a beat, return over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Leaning back 45 degrees and turning it into a row. Pulling the bar behind the neck, which stresses the shoulder. Yanking with the arms instead of the elbows.

name: Close-grip lat pulldown
setup: Attach a V-handle or take a narrow neutral grip. Thigh pad snug, arms straight overhead.
posture: Chest up, slight 15 degree lean back, shoulders pulled down, core braced.
execution: Exhale and pull the handle to the upper chest, elbows driving straight down along the ribs. Squeeze, return over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Rocking the torso to move heavier weight. Stopping short of a full overhead stretch.

name: Wide-grip lat pulldown
setup: Overhand grip roughly 2x shoulder width. Thigh pad snug, arms straight overhead.
posture: Chest up, slight 15 degree lean back, shoulders down away from the ears.
execution: Exhale and pull the bar to the collarbone, elbows flaring down and out. Squeeze, return over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Going so wide the range of motion collapses. Pulling behind the neck. Shrugging at the top of the return.

name: Straight-arm pulldown
setup: Straight bar or rope on a high pulley. Stand a step back, arms straight out in front at shoulder height.
posture: Hinge forward about 15 degrees at the hips, chest up, core braced, knees softly bent.
execution: Keep the elbows locked in a fixed slight bend. Exhale and sweep the bar down in an arc to the thighs. Squeeze the lats a beat, return slowly, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows, which turns it into a triceps pushdown. Standing too upright so the arc is short.

name: Barbell bent-over row
setup: Bar on the floor or in a rack. Overhand grip just wider than shoulder width, feet hip width.
posture: Hinge at the hips to about 45 degrees, back flat, chest up, ribs down, core braced hard. Knees softly bent.
execution: Inhale and brace. Pull the bar to the lower ribs, elbows driving back at 45 degrees. Exhale at the top, lower over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back, which is the main injury risk here. Standing up as you pull. Using the legs to jerk the bar.

name: Pendlay row
setup: Bar on the floor. Overhand grip just wider than shoulder width, torso roughly parallel to the floor.
posture: Flat back, chest up, core braced hard, hips higher than the knees.
execution: Inhale and brace. Explosively pull the bar to the lower ribs. Exhale, then return it fully to the floor and reset before each rep.
commonMistakes: Letting the torso rise as you pull, which defeats the point. Rounding the back to reach the floor between reps.

name: Single-arm dumbbell row
setup: One knee and one hand on a bench, opposite foot planted. Dumbbell hanging at arm's length.
posture: Back flat and roughly parallel to the floor, chest up, hips square, core braced.
execution: Inhale, pull the dumbbell to the hip, elbow driving back close to the ribs. Exhale at the top, lower over 2 to 3 seconds to a full stretch.
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso open to lift heavier. Yanking with the arm instead of leading with the elbow.

name: Seated cable row
setup: Feet on the platform, knees softly bent. Grab the handle and sit up tall with arms straight.
posture: Chest up, shoulders back and down, spine neutral, core braced. Torso stays upright throughout.
execution: Exhale and pull the handle to the navel, elbows driving straight back along the ribs. Squeeze a beat, return over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling to a stretch.
commonMistakes: Rocking the torso back and forth to move weight. Rounding the back at the stretch. Shrugging the shoulders on the pull.

name: T-bar row
setup: Straddle the bar, chest pad set if the machine has one. Take a neutral grip on the handles.
posture: Hinge to about 45 degrees, back flat, chest up, core braced, knees softly bent.
execution: Inhale and brace. Pull the handles to the lower ribs, elbows back at 45 degrees. Exhale at the top, lower over 2 seconds to a full stretch.
commonMistakes: Jerking upright with the hips on every rep. Rounding the lower back under a heavy load.

name: Chest-supported machine row
setup: Set the chest pad so the handles reach comfortably with arms straight. Feet flat.
posture: Chest pressed into the pad, shoulders back and down, core lightly braced.
execution: Exhale and pull the handles back, elbows driving toward the hips. Squeeze a beat, return over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Pushing the chest off the pad to gain leverage. Shrugging at the top of the pull.

name: Inverted row
setup: Bar in a rack at roughly hip height. Hang underneath with an overhand grip 1.5x shoulder width, heels on the floor.
posture: Straight line from head to heels, glutes squeezed, core braced, chest up.
execution: Exhale and pull the chest to the bar, elbows driving back at 45 degrees. Lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling. Lower the bar to make it harder.
commonMistakes: Hips sagging toward the floor. Only pulling halfway up. Craning the neck to touch the bar first.

name: Dumbbell pullover
setup: Lie flat on a bench, or across it with the upper back supported. Hold one dumbbell over the chest with both palms under the top plate.
posture: Ribs down, core braced, feet planted. Hips stay level with the bench.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Inhale and lower the dumbbell in an arc behind the head until you feel a lat and ribcage stretch. Exhale and pull it back over the chest.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop to chase more range. Bending the elbows heavily, which turns it into a triceps move.

name: Kettlebell row
setup: One knee and one hand on a bench, opposite foot planted. Kettlebell hanging at arm's length.
posture: Back flat and roughly parallel to the floor, chest up, hips square, core braced.
execution: Inhale, pull the bell to the hip with the elbow tight to the ribs. Exhale at the top, lower over 2 to 3 seconds to a full stretch.
commonMistakes: Rotating the torso to help the lift. Letting the wrist bend under the bell.

name: Resistance band lat pulldown
setup: Anchor the band overhead. Kneel or sit facing the anchor, a handle in each hand, arms straight up.
posture: Chest up, shoulders down, slight 15 degree lean back, core braced.
execution: Exhale and pull the handles down to shoulder level, elbows driving down and back. Squeeze a beat, return over 2 to 3 seconds against the band.
commonMistakes: Letting the band snap the arms back up. Kneeling too far from the anchor so there is no stretch at the top.

name: Meadows row
setup: One end of a barbell in a landmine sleeve or corner. Stand side-on, stagger the stance, and grip the free end overhand.
posture: Hinge at the hips with a flat back, chest up, free hand braced on the knee, core tight.
execution: Inhale, pull the bar up toward the hip with the elbow high and back. Exhale at the top, lower over 2 to 3 seconds to a full stretch.
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso to add reach. Rounding the back under a heavy loaded end.

name: Machine pullover
setup: Set the seat so the shoulders line up with the machine's pivot. Secure the lap belt if there is one.
posture: Back flat against the pad, chest up, core braced.
execution: Inhale at the top stretch. Pull the handles down in an arc toward the thighs, exhaling. Squeeze the lats a beat, return over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Cutting the top stretch short. Pushing with the arms instead of driving from the lats.

name: Barbell shrug
setup: Bar held in front of the thighs, overhand grip just wider than the hips. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, shoulders back, arms completely straight, core braced. Chin tucked slightly.
execution: Exhale and lift the shoulders straight up toward the ears as high as possible. Hold one second at the top, lower over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Rolling the shoulders in circles, which does nothing extra and grinds the joint. Bending the elbows. Bouncing at the bottom.

name: Dumbbell shrug
setup: A dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, arms straight, core braced, chin slightly tucked.
execution: Exhale and lift the shoulders straight up toward the ears. Hold one second, lower over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Rolling the shoulders. Leaning forward or back to add momentum.

name: Machine shrug
setup: Set the handles so you can stand tall with arms straight. Feet flat and shoulder width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, arms straight, core braced.
execution: Exhale and shrug the shoulders straight up. Hold one second, lower over 2 seconds under control, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees to bounce the weight up. Cutting the range short at the top.

name: Cable shrug
setup: Straight bar on a low pulley, overhand grip. Step back until the cable is taut. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, arms straight, core braced, slight backward lean to counter the cable.
execution: Exhale and shrug straight up. Hold one second, lower over 2 seconds against the cable, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Leaning too far back and turning it into an upright row. Letting the cable drag the shoulders down fast.

name: Trap bar shrug
setup: Stand inside a trap bar, grip the neutral handles, and stand up to a tall position.
posture: Chest up, shoulders back, arms straight, core braced. The neutral grip keeps the load beside you.
execution: Exhale and shrug straight up. Hold one second, lower over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows. Using leg drive to bounce the bar.

name: Kettlebell shrug
setup: A kettlebell in each hand at your sides, arms straight. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, core braced, wrists straight.
execution: Exhale and shrug the shoulders straight up. Hold one second, lower over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Rolling the shoulders. Letting the bells swing forward and back.

name: Face pull
setup: Rope attachment on a pulley set just above head height. Grip both rope ends with thumbs pointing back. Step back until taut.
posture: Split stance, chest up, core braced, slight lean back. Shoulders down away from the ears.
execution: Exhale and pull the rope toward your forehead, splitting the hands wide and driving the elbows high and back. Squeeze a beat, return over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Setting the pulley too low, which turns it into a row. Letting the elbows drop below shoulder height. Using so much weight the torso rocks.

name: Barbell upright row
setup: Bar in front of the thighs, overhand grip at roughly shoulder width. Wider is kinder to the shoulders than narrow.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, core braced, shoulders back.
execution: Exhale and pull the bar up along the body, leading with the elbows, stopping when the upper arms reach shoulder height. Lower over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Pulling above shoulder height with a narrow grip, which pinches the shoulder. Leaning back to heave the bar. Stop the movement if it pinches.

name: Dumbbell upright row
setup: A dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs, palms facing the body. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, core braced, shoulders back and down.
execution: Exhale and pull the dumbbells up along the body, elbows leading, stopping at shoulder height. Lower over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Going above shoulder height. Swinging the torso. Letting the wrists bend sharply at the top.

name: Cable upright row
setup: Straight bar on a low pulley, overhand grip at shoulder width. Stand close so the cable runs vertically.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, core braced, shoulders back.
execution: Exhale and pull the bar up along the body, elbows leading, stopping at shoulder height. Lower over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Standing too far from the pulley so the cable pulls forward. Shrugging hard at the top.

name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
setup: Incline bench at 30 to 45 degrees. Lie chest-down with a dumbbell in each hand hanging straight down.
posture: Chest pressed into the pad, head neutral, shoulders down, core lightly braced.
execution: Exhale and row both dumbbells toward the hips, elbows driving back and close. Squeeze a beat, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad. Flaring the elbows straight out, which shifts work to the rear delts only.

name: Seal row
setup: Lie chest-down on a bench raised high enough that the bar clears the floor. Grip the bar with arms hanging straight.
posture: Chest and hips on the bench throughout, head neutral, core lightly braced.
execution: Exhale and row the bar to the lower ribs, elbows driving back. Squeeze a beat, lower over 2 to 3 seconds to a full stretch, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench to cheat, which is the whole reason this variation exists. Bouncing the bar off the floor.

name: Prone Y-raise
setup: Incline bench at 30 degrees. Lie chest-down holding light dumbbells, arms hanging straight down.
posture: Chest on the pad, head neutral, shoulders pulled down away from the ears.
execution: Thumbs up. Exhale and raise both arms out and up into a Y shape until level with the ears. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Going too heavy, which turns it into a shrug. Shrugging the shoulders up instead of keeping them down.

name: Farmer's carry
setup: A heavy dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in. Stand tall before moving.
posture: Chest up, shoulders back and down, ribs stacked over the hips, core braced hard. Head neutral, eyes forward.
execution: Walk at a steady controlled pace for the set duration. Breathe in a shallow rhythm rather than holding your breath. Set the weights down deliberately.
commonMistakes: Leaning back or to one side. Shrugging the shoulders up. Holding the breath for the whole carry.

name: Band pull-apart
setup: Hold a light band with both hands, arms straight out in front at shoulder height, hands shoulder width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, ribs down, shoulders back and down, core braced.
execution: Exhale and pull the band apart until the arms are out to the sides, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Hold one second, return over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows. Letting the band snap back. Using a band so heavy the shoulders shrug up.

name: Back extension
setup: Set the hip pad just below the hip bones so the hips can hinge freely. Ankles secured, feet on the platform.
posture: Spine neutral from head to tail, chest up, core braced, arms crossed on the chest.
execution: Inhale and lower by hinging at the hips until you feel a hamstring stretch, roughly 60 to 90 degrees. Exhale and rise until the body is straight.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending past a straight line at the top, which compresses the lower back. Rounding the spine on the way down instead of hinging.

name: Machine back extension
setup: Set the seat and pad so the pad sits across the upper back and the pivot lines up with your hips.
posture: Chest up, spine neutral, core braced, feet flat.
execution: Inhale, then push back against the pad to a straight torso, exhaling. Pause one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds under control.
commonMistakes: Slamming back into full extension. Letting the weight stack drop and yank you forward.

name: Conventional deadlift
setup: Bar over mid-foot, roughly 2cm from the shins. Feet hip width. Hinge and grip just outside the legs.
posture: Chest up, flat back, shoulders slightly ahead of the bar, hips higher than the knees, lats squeezed as if holding paper under the armpits. Core braced hard.
execution: Inhale and brace. Push the floor away with the legs, keeping the bar dragging up the shins. Stand tall, exhale at the top. Hinge back down under control.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back, which is the main injury risk. Letting the hips shoot up first so it becomes a stiff-leg pull. Leaning back at the top.

name: Trap bar deadlift
setup: Stand inside the trap bar, feet hip width, centred between the handles. Hinge and take the neutral grip.
posture: Chest up, flat back, hips slightly higher than the knees, shoulders down, core braced hard.
execution: Inhale and brace. Push the floor away and stand tall, exhaling at the top. Hinge back down under control, touching the plates lightly.
commonMistakes: Standing too far forward or back inside the frame. Rounding the back. Jerking the bar off the floor.

name: Barbell good morning
setup: Bar racked across the upper back as in a squat. Feet hip to shoulder width. Start light, this one punishes ego.
posture: Chest up, flat back, core braced hard, knees softly bent and held there.
execution: Inhale and brace. Hinge at the hips, pushing them straight back, until the torso reaches roughly 45 to 70 degrees or the hamstrings stop you. Exhale as you drive the hips forward to stand.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees more as you descend, which turns it into a squat. Rounding the back. Going far heavier than the hamstrings can control.

name: Rack pull
setup: Bar set on rack pins at roughly knee height. Feet hip width, grip just outside the legs.
posture: Chest up, flat back, shoulders over or slightly behind the bar, lats engaged, core braced hard.
execution: Inhale and brace. Drive the hips forward and stand tall, exhaling at the top. Lower under control back to the pins and let it settle before the next rep.
commonMistakes: Loading far more than you can control because the range is short. Yanking off the pins. Leaning back at lockout.

name: Reverse hyperextension
setup: Lie chest-down on the machine, hips at the edge of the pad, ankles behind the roller. Grip the handles.
posture: Chest and ribs on the pad, core braced, spine neutral, head in line with the torso.
execution: Inhale at the bottom. Exhale and raise the legs until they are level with the torso, squeezing the glutes. Lower over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Swinging the legs and using momentum. Lifting past horizontal into lower-back hyperextension.

name: Superman
setup: Lie face down on the floor, arms extended overhead, legs straight, forehead resting down.
posture: Neck neutral, core lightly engaged, hips pressed into the floor.
execution: Exhale and lift the arms, chest and legs a few inches off the floor at the same time. Hold for 2 seconds, lower slowly and inhale.
commonMistakes: Cranking the neck up to look forward. Lifting so high the lower back pinches.

name: Bird dog
setup: On all fours, hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips. Spine neutral.
posture: Flat back like a tabletop, core braced, hips level, neck in line with the spine.
execution: Exhale and extend the right arm forward and the left leg back until both are level with the torso. Hold 2 seconds, return slowly, inhale, then switch sides.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips rotate open as the leg lifts. Lifting the limbs above shoulder or hip height and arching the lower back.

name: Barbell overhead press
setup: Bar racked at upper-chest height. Grip just outside shoulder width, elbows slightly in front of the bar. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, ribs down, glutes and core braced hard so the lower back doesn't arch. Chest up, chin tucked back out of the bar path.
execution: Inhale and brace. Press the bar straight up past the face, then push the head slightly forward once it clears. Exhale at lockout with the bar over mid-foot. Lower to the collarbone over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Leaning back into a standing incline press. Pressing around the face instead of tucking the chin. Letting the ribs flare and the lower back arch.

name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
setup: Upright bench with the back pad near vertical. Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward, elbows at about 45 degrees to the torso.
posture: Back against the pad, ribs down, core braced, feet flat and driving into the floor.
execution: Inhale, press the dumbbells up and slightly together until the arms are nearly straight. Exhale at the top, lower over 2 seconds to ear height.
commonMistakes: Clanging the dumbbells together at the top. Flaring the elbows straight out to 90 degrees. Arching the lower back off the pad.

name: Standing dumbbell shoulder press
setup: Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward, elbows at about 45 degrees. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, ribs down, glutes and core braced hard, chest up.
execution: Inhale and brace. Press up and slightly together until the arms are nearly straight, exhaling. Lower over 2 seconds to ear height.
commonMistakes: Using a leg dip to start the press, which makes it a push press. Leaning back as the set gets hard.

name: Machine shoulder press
setup: Set the seat so the handles sit at roughly shoulder or ear height. Feet flat.
posture: Back against the pad, ribs down, core braced, chest up.
execution: Inhale, press the handles up until the arms are nearly straight without locking hard. Exhale on the press, lower over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Seat set too low, which forces an awkward overhead angle. Slamming into lockout.

name: Smith machine shoulder press
setup: Bench set upright under the bar so the fixed path runs just in front of the face. Grip just outside shoulder width.
posture: Back against the pad, ribs down, core braced, chin tucked out of the bar path.
execution: Unrack with a wrist twist. Inhale, press straight up to nearly locked, exhaling. Lower to chin height over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Placing the bench so the bar path scrapes the nose. Letting the fixed path do the stabilising while the core goes slack.

name: Arnold press
setup: Seated upright. Start with dumbbells at chest height, palms facing you, elbows tucked in front.
posture: Back against the pad, ribs down, core braced, chest up.
execution: Inhale. As you press up, rotate the palms outward so they face forward at the top. Exhale at lockout. Reverse the rotation on the way down over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Rushing the rotation so it happens all at once at the top. Using heavy weight, which makes the rotation jerky and hard on the shoulder.

name: Push press
setup: Bar racked on the front delts at collarbone height, grip just outside shoulder width. Feet hip width.
posture: Chest up, ribs down, core braced hard, weight through the mid-foot.
execution: Inhale and brace. Dip the knees about 10cm, then drive explosively through the legs and press the bar overhead, exhaling at lockout. Lower to the shoulders under control.
commonMistakes: Dipping too deep, which turns it into a squat. Letting the chest fall forward during the dip. Leaning back at lockout.

name: Dumbbell front raise
setup: A dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs, palms facing the body. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, ribs down, core braced, shoulders back and down.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise one or both arms forward to shoulder height, no higher. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to throw the weight up. Going above shoulder height, where the traps take over.

name: Barbell front raise
setup: Bar held in front of the thighs, overhand grip at shoulder width. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, ribs down, core braced hard, glutes squeezed.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the bar forward to shoulder height. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Leaning back to counterbalance the bar. Using momentum from the hips.

name: Cable front raise
setup: Straight bar or single handle on a low pulley behind you. Step forward until the cable is taut.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, ribs down, core braced, slight forward lean to counter the cable.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the handle forward to shoulder height. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds against the cable.
commonMistakes: Letting the cable drag the arm down fast. Rocking the torso to start each rep.

name: Plate front raise
setup: Hold a weight plate at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions with both hands, in front of the thighs.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, ribs down, core braced, shoulders back.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the plate forward to shoulder height. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Raising above shoulder height. Leaning back as the plate gets further from the body.

name: Landmine shoulder press
setup: One barbell end in a landmine sleeve or corner. Hold the free end at shoulder height, half-kneeling or standing.
posture: Chest up, ribs down, hips square, core braced hard. Torso stays vertical.
execution: Inhale, press the bar up and forward along its natural arc until the arm is nearly straight, exhaling. Lower over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Leaning back to help. Letting the hips rotate toward the pressing arm.

name: Pike push-up
setup: Hands flat on the floor slightly wider than the shoulders, feet walked in so the hips are high and the body forms an inverted V.
posture: Hips high, back flat, core braced, head between the arms and neck neutral.
execution: Inhale and lower until the crown of the head is just off the floor, elbows at 45 degrees. Press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop so it becomes a regular push-up. Banging the head on the floor. Flaring the elbows straight out.

name: Kettlebell overhead press
setup: Clean one kettlebell to the rack position at the shoulder, bell resting on the back of the forearm, elbow tucked.
posture: Stand tall, ribs down, glutes and core braced, wrist straight and stacked over the elbow.
execution: Inhale and brace. Press the bell up, letting the palm rotate to face forward at lockout, exhaling. Lower over 2 to 3 seconds to the rack.
commonMistakes: Letting the wrist bend back under the bell. Leaning away from the working side.

name: Band overhead press
setup: Stand on the middle of the band, a handle in each hand at shoulder height, palms forward.
posture: Stand tall, ribs down, core and glutes braced, chest up.
execution: Inhale, press up until the arms are nearly straight, exhaling at the top where band tension peaks. Lower over 2 to 3 seconds against the band.
commonMistakes: Letting the band snap the arms down. Arching the lower back as tension increases near lockout.

name: Dumbbell lateral raise
setup: A light dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, ribs down, shoulders pulled down away from the ears, core braced.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder height, leading with the elbows. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to heave the weights up. Going above shoulder height, which hands the work to the traps. Shrugging as you lift.

name: Seated dumbbell lateral raise
setup: Sit on the end of a bench, feet flat, a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
posture: Sit tall, chest up, shoulders down away from the ears, core braced. Seated position removes the option to swing.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the arms out to shoulder height. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Leaning the torso back to cheat. Shrugging at the top.

name: Cable lateral raise
setup: Single handle on the lowest pulley. Stand side-on, take the handle in the far hand across the body.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, shoulders down, core braced, free hand on the frame for balance.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the arm out to shoulder height. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds against the cable.
commonMistakes: Letting the cable pull the arm down fast. Leaning away from the machine to gain leverage.

name: Leaning cable lateral raise
setup: Grip the machine upright with one hand and lean away so the body tilts about 20 degrees. Handle from the low pulley in the far hand.
posture: Body in a straight line from the anchoring hand to the feet, core braced, shoulder pulled down.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the arm out to shoulder height. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Swinging the whole body in and out from the upright. Shrugging at the top of the raise.

name: Machine lateral raise
setup: Set the seat so the shoulder joints line up with the machine's pivot points. Arms against the pads.
posture: Sit tall, back against the pad, chest up, shoulders down away from the ears.
execution: Exhale and press the pads out and up to shoulder height, leading with the elbows. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Seat set too high or low so the pivot misses the shoulder. Shrugging into the pads.

name: Band lateral raise
setup: Stand on the middle of a light band, a handle in each hand at your sides.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, shoulders down, core braced.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the arms out to shoulder height where tension peaks. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Using a band so heavy the last few degrees force a shrug. Letting the band snap the arms down.

name: Kettlebell lateral raise
setup: A light kettlebell in each hand at your sides, bells hanging below the handles.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, shoulders down, core braced, wrists straight.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the arms out to shoulder height. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Letting the bells swing forward. Going heavier than the offset load allows and shrugging.

name: Plate lateral raise
setup: A light plate in each hand held by the rim, arms at your sides.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, shoulders down away from the ears, core braced.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the arms out to shoulder height. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Gripping so hard the forearms fatigue first. Raising above shoulder height.

name: Lu raise
setup: Very light dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in. Feet hip width. Start lighter than you think.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, ribs down, core braced hard, shoulders down.
execution: Exhale and sweep the arms out and all the way overhead until the dumbbells nearly touch above the head. Lower over 3 seconds along the same path, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Using anything but very light weight. Arching the lower back as the arms pass overhead. Rushing the lowering phase.

name: Cable Y-raise
setup: Two low pulleys, handles crossed so the left hand takes the right cable and vice versa. Step back until taut.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, ribs down, core braced, shoulders pulled down.
execution: Thumbs up. Exhale and sweep both arms out and up into a Y at about 45 degrees above the shoulders. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up into the ears. Using enough weight that the torso leans back.

name: Barbell overhead carry
setup: Press a light barbell overhead with a grip just outside shoulder width. Lock the arms before you move.
posture: Arms locked straight with the bar over mid-foot, ribs down, glutes and core braced hard, chest up, eyes forward.
execution: Walk at a slow controlled pace for the set duration, breathing shallow and steady. Lower the bar carefully to the rack or shoulders at the end.
commonMistakes: Letting the ribs flare and the bar drift behind the head. Holding the breath. Starting heavier than you can control overhead.

name: Bent-over dumbbell reverse fly
setup: A light dumbbell in each hand. Hinge at the hips until the torso is roughly parallel to the floor, arms hanging straight down.
posture: Flat back, chest up, core braced, knees softly bent, head in line with the spine.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the arms out to the sides until level with the torso, squeezing the shoulder blades. Lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Standing up as you raise. Using heavy weight so the movement becomes a row. Rounding the lower back.

name: Chest-supported dumbbell reverse fly
setup: Incline bench at 30 to 45 degrees. Lie chest-down with light dumbbells hanging straight down.
posture: Chest on the pad, head neutral, shoulders pulled down away from the ears.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder level. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad. Bending the elbows and rowing instead of flying.

name: Reverse pec deck
setup: Turn to face the pec deck's back pad. Set the handles so the arms start straight out in front at shoulder height.
posture: Chest against the pad, sit tall, shoulders down away from the ears, core lightly braced.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and sweep the handles out and back until level with the torso. Squeeze one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Setting the start too far back, which overstretches the shoulder. Shrugging during the squeeze.

name: Machine rear delt fly
setup: Set the seat so the handles sit at shoulder height with the chest against the pad.
posture: Chest on the pad, sit tall, shoulders pulled down, core lightly braced.
execution: Exhale and drive the handles back in a wide arc until level with the torso. Squeeze one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Pushing the chest off the pad for leverage. Bending the elbows into a row.

name: Cable reverse fly
setup: Two pulleys at shoulder height, cables crossed so each hand takes the opposite cable. Step back until taut.
posture: Stand tall or hinge slightly, chest up, shoulders down, core braced, split stance for stability.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and sweep the arms out and back in a wide arc. Squeeze one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Letting the cables pull the arms forward fast. Bending the elbows and turning it into a row.

name: Reverse cable crossover
setup: Two pulleys at shoulder height, handles crossed in front. Step back until there is tension, feet in a split stance.
posture: Chest up, shoulders down away from the ears, core braced, torso still.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and pull the arms apart and back until level with the torso. Squeeze one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso to add range. Shrugging at the end of the pull.

name: Rear delt cable row to neck
setup: Rope on a pulley set at upper-chest height. Grip both ends, step back until taut, split stance.
posture: Chest up, shoulders down, core braced, slight lean back.
execution: Exhale and pull the rope toward the neck with the elbows high and flared out to the sides. Squeeze one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Dropping the elbows, which turns it into a normal row. Using enough weight that the torso rocks back.

name: Prone incline rear delt raise
setup: Incline bench at 30 degrees. Lie chest-down with light dumbbells hanging straight down, palms facing back.
posture: Chest on the pad, head neutral, shoulders pulled down.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and raise the arms straight out to the sides to shoulder level. Hold one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Going heavy and swinging. Letting the arms drift back toward the hips instead of straight out.

name: Band reverse fly
setup: Hold a band with both hands, arms straight out in front at shoulder height, hands roughly shoulder width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, ribs down, shoulders down, core braced.
execution: Fixed slight elbow bend. Exhale and pull the arms out and back until wide, squeezing the shoulder blades. Hold one second, return over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows. Letting the band snap back. Shrugging as the tension rises.

name: Kettlebell high pull
setup: One kettlebell on the floor between the feet, stance slightly wider than the hips. Hinge and grip the handle.
posture: Flat back, chest up, core braced, shoulders down.
execution: Hinge and swing the bell back, then drive the hips forward explosively. As it rises, pull the elbow high and back to chest height, exhaling. Let it swing back down and inhale.
commonMistakes: Pulling with the arm instead of driving from the hips. Letting the bell get ahead of the elbow. Rounding the back at the bottom of the swing.

name: Barbell curl
setup: Bar held at arm's length in front of the thighs, underhand grip at shoulder width. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, shoulders back and down, elbows pinned to the sides of the ribs, core braced.
execution: Exhale and curl the bar up to chest height, keeping the elbows fixed in place. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso and using the lower back. Letting the elbows drift forward, which brings in the front delts. Dropping the bar fast.

name: EZ-bar curl
setup: EZ bar at arm's length, hands on the angled sections at shoulder width, palms up.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, elbows pinned to the ribs, core braced. The angled grip is easier on the wrists.
execution: Exhale and curl to chest height with the elbows fixed. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Rocking the torso. Elbows travelling forward at the top.

name: Dumbbell curl
setup: A dumbbell in each hand at arm's length, palms facing forward. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, shoulders back, elbows pinned to the ribs, core braced.
execution: Exhale and curl both dumbbells to shoulder height. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds to full arm extension, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Swinging the weights up. Stopping short of full extension at the bottom, which cuts the range.

name: Alternating dumbbell curl
setup: A dumbbell in each hand at arm's length, palms facing in. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, elbows pinned to the ribs, core braced, torso completely still.
execution: Exhale and curl one dumbbell up, rotating the palm to face up as it rises. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, then switch.
commonMistakes: Leaning side to side with each rep. Starting the next arm before the first has fully lowered.

name: Hammer curl
setup: A dumbbell in each hand at arm's length, palms facing in toward the thighs. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, elbows pinned to the ribs, wrists straight, core braced.
execution: Keep the palms facing in throughout. Exhale and curl to shoulder height. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Letting the palms rotate up, which turns it into a normal curl. Swinging the torso.

name: Incline dumbbell curl
setup: Bench set to about 60 degrees. Sit back with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down behind the torso line.
posture: Back against the pad, chest up, shoulders back, upper arms hanging still throughout.
execution: Exhale and curl both dumbbells up without letting the elbows travel forward. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds to a full stretch.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows swing forward, which removes the stretch that makes this variation useful. Lifting the shoulders off the pad.

name: Concentration curl
setup: Sit on a bench, feet wide. Rest the back of the working upper arm against the inside of the same-side thigh, dumbbell hanging.
posture: Torso leaned forward with a flat back, chest up, upper arm locked against the thigh.
execution: Exhale and curl the dumbbell up toward the opposite shoulder. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds to full extension, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Pushing with the leg to help the curl. Rounding the back over the working arm.

name: Spider curl
setup: Incline bench at about 45 degrees. Lie chest-down with arms hanging straight down over the top edge.
posture: Chest on the pad, head neutral, upper arms perpendicular to the floor and locked there.
execution: Exhale and curl the weight up toward the shoulders. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds to a full stretch, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad. Letting the upper arms swing back on the descent.

name: Zottman curl
setup: A dumbbell in each hand at arm's length, palms facing forward. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, elbows pinned to the ribs, core braced.
execution: Exhale and curl up with palms up. At the top, rotate the palms to face down, then lower over 3 seconds in that overhand position. Rotate back at the bottom.
commonMistakes: Rushing the overhand descent, which is the part that trains the forearms. Going too heavy to control the rotation.

name: Preacher curl
setup: Set the preacher bench so the top of the pad sits under the armpits. EZ bar or barbell, underhand grip at shoulder width.
posture: Chest against the pad, shoulders down, upper arms flat on the pad throughout.
execution: Exhale and curl the bar up to chest height. Squeeze one second, lower over 3 seconds until the arms are almost straight, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Letting the arms snap straight at the bottom under load, which strains the elbow. Lifting the armpits off the pad.

name: Machine preacher curl
setup: Set the seat so the upper arms rest flat on the pad with the elbows level with the pivot. Grip the handles.
posture: Chest against the pad, shoulders down, upper arms flat throughout.
execution: Exhale and curl the handles up. Squeeze one second, lower over 3 seconds to nearly straight arms, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Elbows misaligned with the pivot. Slamming the stack down at the bottom.

name: Cable curl
setup: Straight or EZ bar on the lowest pulley. Stand a step back, arms hanging straight, underhand grip at shoulder width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, elbows pinned to the ribs, core braced, slight forward lean to counter the cable.
execution: Exhale and curl the bar to chest height. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds against constant cable tension.
commonMistakes: Letting the cable drag the arms straight fast. Stepping so far back that the elbows get pulled behind the torso.

name: Cable rope hammer curl
setup: Rope on the lowest pulley. Stand a step back, a rope end in each hand, palms facing in.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, elbows pinned to the ribs, wrists straight, core braced.
execution: Keep the palms facing each other throughout. Exhale and curl up to shoulder height, spreading the rope ends slightly at the top. Lower over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Rotating the palms up. Letting the elbows drift forward as fatigue sets in.

name: Bayesian cable curl
setup: Single handle on the lowest pulley. Face away from the machine and step forward so the arm hangs behind the torso line.
posture: Stand tall in a split stance, chest up, upper arm fixed behind the body, core braced.
execution: Exhale and curl the handle up without letting the elbow travel forward. Squeeze one second, lower over 3 seconds to a deep stretch, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbow swing forward, which removes the behind-the-body stretch. Standing too close so there is no tension at the bottom.

name: Drag curl
setup: Bar at arm's length in front of the thighs, underhand grip at shoulder width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, shoulders back and down, core braced.
execution: Drag the bar straight up the front of the body, letting the elbows travel backward rather than staying pinned. Exhale on the way up, lower over 2 to 3 seconds along the same path.
commonMistakes: Letting the bar swing away from the body, which makes it a normal curl. Using heavy weight, since the range here is short.

name: 21s barbell curl
setup: Bar at arm's length, underhand grip at shoulder width. Feet hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, elbows pinned to the ribs, core braced.
execution: Do 7 reps from the bottom to halfway, then 7 from halfway to the top, then 7 full-range reps. Exhale on each lift, breathe steadily throughout. Use lighter weight than a normal curl.
commonMistakes: Using your usual curl weight and failing halfway through. Swinging the torso once the burn arrives.

name: Kettlebell curl
setup: A kettlebell in each hand at arm's length, palms forward, bells hanging below the handles.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, elbows pinned to the ribs, wrists straight, core braced.
execution: Exhale and curl to shoulder height. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Letting the wrists bend back under the offset weight. Swinging the bells up.

name: Band curl
setup: Stand on the middle of the band, a handle in each hand at arm's length, palms forward.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, elbows pinned to the ribs, core braced.
execution: Exhale and curl up to shoulder height where band tension peaks. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds against the band.
commonMistakes: Letting the band snap the arms straight. Leaning back as tension increases near the top.

name: Cable pushdown (straight bar)
setup: Straight bar on a high pulley set at upper-chest height. Overhand grip at shoulder width. Step back half a pace.
posture: Stand tall with a slight 10 degree forward lean, chest up, elbows pinned to the sides of the ribs, core braced.
execution: Exhale and push the bar down until the arms are straight, keeping the elbows fixed. Squeeze one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds until the forearms reach about 90 degrees.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows drift forward and away from the ribs. Leaning the whole bodyweight onto the bar. Shrugging the shoulders on the push.

name: Cable rope pushdown
setup: Rope on a high pulley at upper-chest height. Grip both ends with palms facing in. Step back half a pace.
posture: Stand tall with a slight forward lean, chest up, elbows pinned to the ribs, core braced.
execution: Exhale and push down, spreading the rope ends apart at the bottom for an extra squeeze. Hold one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds.
commonMistakes: Elbows flaring out and forward. Turning it into a shoulder push by leaning in.

name: Reverse-grip cable pushdown
setup: Straight bar on a high pulley, underhand grip at shoulder width. Step back half a pace.
posture: Stand tall, slight forward lean, elbows pinned to the ribs, wrists straight and firm, core braced.
execution: Exhale and push the bar down to straight arms. Squeeze one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds. Use lighter weight than the overhand version.
commonMistakes: Using overhand-grip weight and losing the wrists. Letting the elbows travel forward.

name: Overhead cable triceps extension
setup: Rope on the lowest pulley. Face away from the machine, rope behind the head, elbows pointing forward and up.
posture: Split stance, chest up, ribs down, core braced hard so the lower back doesn't arch. Upper arms stay beside the ears.
execution: Exhale and extend the arms overhead until straight, keeping the elbows in place. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds to a deep stretch, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows flare wide. Arching the lower back as the arms extend. Dropping the upper arms forward.

name: Cable triceps kickback
setup: Single handle on the lowest pulley. Hinge forward until the torso is roughly parallel to the floor, upper arm tucked against the ribs.
posture: Flat back, chest up, core braced, upper arm locked in place parallel to the floor.
execution: Exhale and extend the forearm back until the arm is straight. Squeeze one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Letting the upper arm drop or swing. Standing up as you extend.

name: EZ-bar skull crusher
setup: Lie flat on a bench, EZ bar held over the chest with an overhand grip on the angled sections, arms straight.
posture: Shoulder blades on the bench, ribs down, core braced, upper arms angled slightly back so tension stays on the triceps.
execution: Inhale and lower the bar toward the forehead or just behind the head by bending only at the elbows. Stop just short of contact, then extend and exhale.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows wide, which strains them. Moving the upper arms instead of hinging only at the elbow. Going too heavy on a joint-sensitive move.

name: Close-grip bench press
setup: Flat bench, overhand grip at roughly shoulder width. Not narrower, which just hurts the wrists.
posture: Shoulder blades retracted, chest up, feet flat, elbows tucked to about 20 degrees from the torso.
execution: Inhale and lower the bar to the lower chest with the elbows tucked close. Press up and exhale, driving through the triceps.
commonMistakes: Gripping so narrow the wrists bend painfully. Flaring the elbows, which turns it back into a chest press.

name: JM press
setup: Flat bench, barbell with an overhand grip at shoulder width, bar held over the chest.
posture: Shoulder blades retracted, chest up, feet flat, elbows tucked. Start very light, this is a technical lift.
execution: Inhale and lower the bar toward the upper chest and throat by bending the elbows and letting the upper arms travel slightly back. Stop just above the collarbone, then press and exhale.
commonMistakes: Treating it as a close-grip bench, which loses the point. Going heavy before the groove is learned, with the bar tracking near the throat.

name: Dumbbell overhead triceps extension
setup: Sit or stand holding one dumbbell with both hands, pressed overhead. Palms cupping the top plate.
posture: Chest up, ribs down, core braced hard, upper arms beside the ears and locked there.
execution: Inhale and lower the dumbbell behind the head by bending only the elbows, until you feel a triceps stretch. Exhale and extend back up.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows flare wide. Arching the lower back to help. Moving the upper arms instead of hinging at the elbow.

name: Single-arm dumbbell overhead extension
setup: Sit or stand with one dumbbell pressed overhead in one hand, palm facing forward.
posture: Chest up, ribs down, core braced, upper arm beside the ear. Free hand can support the working elbow.
execution: Inhale and lower the dumbbell behind the head by bending the elbow. Exhale and extend back to straight over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Letting the torso lean away from the working arm. Elbow drifting outward.

name: Lying dumbbell triceps extension
setup: Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand pressed above the chest, palms facing in.
posture: Shoulder blades on the bench, ribs down, core braced, upper arms angled slightly back.
execution: Inhale and lower the dumbbells toward the ears by bending only the elbows. Exhale and extend back up over the chest.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows out. Letting the upper arms swing back and turning it into a pullover.

name: Dumbbell triceps kickback
setup: One knee and hand on a bench, or hinged forward standing. Dumbbell in hand, upper arm tucked against the ribs and parallel to the floor.
posture: Flat back, chest up, core braced, upper arm locked in place.
execution: Exhale and extend the forearm back until the arm is straight. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Swinging the dumbbell back with momentum. Letting the upper arm drop below parallel.

name: Machine triceps extension
setup: Set the seat so the elbows line up with the machine's pivot and rest on the pad.
posture: Back against the pad, chest up, elbows fixed on the pad throughout, core lightly braced.
execution: Exhale and extend the arms until straight. Squeeze one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds under control.
commonMistakes: Elbows sliding off the pad. Slamming the stack down between reps.

name: Assisted triceps dip machine
setup: Set the assistance weight, kneel or stand on the pad, hands on the parallel bars.
posture: Torso upright and vertical, chest up, shoulders down away from the ears, elbows tucked close to the ribs.
execution: Inhale and lower until the upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor. Press up and exhale. Less assistance weight means you are getting stronger.
commonMistakes: Leaning the torso forward, which shifts the work to the chest. Bouncing off the pad.

name: Bench triceps dip
setup: Sit on a bench, hands gripping the edge beside the hips. Slide the hips forward off the bench, legs out in front.
posture: Torso upright and close to the bench, chest up, shoulders pulled down away from the ears, elbows pointing straight back.
execution: Inhale and lower until the elbows reach about 90 degrees. Press up and exhale. Stop if the front of the shoulder pinches.
commonMistakes: Dropping far below 90 degrees, which strains the shoulder. Letting the hips drift away from the bench. Flaring the elbows out.

name: Parallel bar dip (upright)
setup: Parallel bars, hands at your sides. Push up to a supported start with the arms straight.
posture: Torso vertical, chest up, shoulders pulled down away from the ears, elbows tucked close to the ribs, ankles crossed.
execution: Inhale and lower until the upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping the torso upright. Press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Leaning forward, which turns it into a chest dip. Going deeper than shoulder comfort allows. Shrugging at the bottom.

name: Diamond push-up
setup: Hands flat on the floor under the chest, index fingers and thumbs touching to form a triangle.
posture: Straight line from head to heels, core braced, glutes squeezed, elbows tracking back close to the ribs.
execution: Inhale and lower until the chest touches the hands. Press up and exhale.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows straight out, which is hard on the wrists and elbows. Hips sagging as the movement gets tough.

name: Kettlebell overhead extension
setup: Hold one kettlebell with both hands by the horns, pressed overhead, bell hanging behind the head.
posture: Chest up, ribs down, core braced hard, upper arms beside the ears, wrists straight.
execution: Inhale and lower the bell behind the head by bending only the elbows. Exhale and extend back up over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Letting the wrists bend back. Arching the lower back as the bell drops behind.

name: Band triceps pushdown
setup: Anchor a band overhead. Grip both ends, elbows pinned to the ribs, forearms at about 90 degrees.
posture: Stand tall, slight forward lean, chest up, elbows fixed at the sides, core braced.
execution: Exhale and push down to straight arms where band tension peaks. Squeeze one second, return over 2 to 3 seconds against the band.
commonMistakes: Letting the band pull the forearms up fast. Elbows drifting forward as tension increases.

name: Barbell wrist curl
setup: Sit on a bench, forearms resting on the thighs, wrists just past the knees, palms up. Bar held loosely.
posture: Sit tall with a flat back, forearms flat and still on the thighs throughout.
execution: Let the bar roll to the fingertips, then exhale and curl it up by closing the fingers and flexing the wrist. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Lifting the forearms off the thighs. Using so much weight the wrists can't complete the range.

name: Barbell reverse wrist curl
setup: Sit on a bench, forearms on the thighs, wrists just past the knees, palms facing down. Bar held overhand.
posture: Sit tall with a flat back, forearms flat and still throughout.
execution: Exhale and lift the back of the hands upward as far as they will go. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Going as heavy as the palms-up version, which the wrist extensors cannot handle. Lifting the forearms off the thighs.

name: Behind-the-back barbell wrist curl
setup: Stand with a barbell held behind the back at arm's length, palms facing back, grip at hip width.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, shoulders back and down, arms straight and still.
execution: Let the bar roll to the fingertips, then exhale and curl it up by flexing the wrists. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to help. Letting the bar roll out of the fingers entirely.

name: EZ-bar reverse curl
setup: EZ bar held at arm's length in front of the thighs, overhand grip on the angled sections.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, elbows pinned to the ribs, wrists straight and locked, core braced.
execution: Exhale and curl the bar up to chest height with the palms staying down. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 to 3 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Using normal curl weight, which the overhand grip cannot support. Letting the wrists collapse backward.

name: Dumbbell wrist curl
setup: Sit on a bench, one forearm resting on the thigh, wrist just past the knee, palm up. Dumbbell held loosely.
posture: Sit tall with a flat back, forearm flat and still on the thigh.
execution: Let the dumbbell roll to the fingertips, then exhale and curl it up by closing the fingers and flexing the wrist. Lower over 2 seconds.
commonMistakes: Lifting the forearm off the thigh. Skipping the fingertip roll, which halves the range.

name: Dumbbell reverse wrist curl
setup: Sit on a bench, one forearm on the thigh, wrist just past the knee, palm facing down.
posture: Sit tall with a flat back, forearm flat and still.
execution: Exhale and lift the back of the hand upward as far as it will go. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Going too heavy for the small extensor muscles. Rotating the forearm to cheat the movement.

name: Cable wrist curl
setup: Straight bar on the lowest pulley. Kneel or sit with the forearms resting on a bench, wrists past the edge, palms up.
posture: Forearms flat and still on the bench, back flat, shoulders relaxed.
execution: Exhale and curl the bar up by flexing the wrists against constant cable tension. Squeeze one second, lower over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Lifting the forearms off the bench. Positioning so far from the pulley that the cable pulls at an angle.

name: Kettlebell farmer hold
setup: A heavy kettlebell in each hand at your sides, arms straight. Stand tall before starting the clock.
posture: Chest up, shoulders back and down, ribs stacked over the hips, core braced hard, wrists straight.
execution: Hold still for the set duration, gripping hard. Breathe in a shallow steady rhythm rather than holding your breath. Set the bells down deliberately.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up. Letting the bells drift forward. Holding the breath for the whole set.

name: Dead hang
setup: Grip a pull-up bar overhand at roughly shoulder width. Step off and let the body hang.
posture: Arms straight, shoulders active and pulled slightly down rather than fully loose. Ribs down, core lightly braced so the legs don't swing.
execution: Hang for the set duration, gripping hard. Breathe slow and steady. Step down under control rather than dropping.
commonMistakes: Hanging completely limp with shoulders in the ears. Swinging. Dropping off the bar from height.

name: Plate pinch hold
setup: Stand holding one or two smooth weight plates pinched between the thumb and fingers, arms at your sides.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, shoulders back and down, arms straight and still.
execution: Pinch hard and hold for the set duration. Breathe steadily. Set the plates down under control before the grip fully fails.
commonMistakes: Letting the plates slip and drop on your feet. Holding to complete failure over a bare floor.

name: Wrist roller
setup: Hold the roller bar out in front at shoulder height with both hands, weight hanging from the cord.
posture: Stand tall, chest up, arms straight out in front and held level, core braced.
execution: Roll the cord up by alternating wrist flexion hand over hand, then reverse it down slowly. Breathe steadily throughout, don't hold your breath.
commonMistakes: Letting the arms drop as the shoulders fatigue. Letting the weight unwind fast instead of lowering it under control.

name: Band wrist extension
setup: Loop a light band around the fingers of one hand, other end anchored or held. Forearm resting on a thigh or bench, palm down.
posture: Forearm flat and still, wrist just past the edge, shoulders relaxed.
execution: Exhale and open the fingers and extend the wrist upward against the band. Hold one second, return over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Using a band so heavy the forearm lifts to help. Rushing the return.

name: Machine gripper
setup: Set the handle spacing so the hand can open comfortably at the start. Grip with the whole hand.
posture: Sit or stand tall, wrist straight and in line with the forearm, shoulder relaxed.
execution: Exhale and squeeze the handle fully closed. Hold one second, open slowly over 2 seconds, inhaling.
commonMistakes: Letting the wrist bend to add leverage. Snapping the handle open on the return.

name: Crunch
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent at about 90 degrees, feet flat. Hands lightly behind the ears or crossed on the chest.
posture: Lower back stays in contact with the floor, chin a fist's width from the chest, neck relaxed.
